title: Delegated Pricing Approval & Audit Playbook for Enterprise Contracts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Create an operational playbook that lets account teams approve negotiated discounts and contract flex within predefined guardrails while producing an auditable trail for finance, legal and security questionnaire responses. Scope includes delegation rules, automated recording (Salesforce/Stripe), a canonical pricing catalog update process, and escalation paths for exceptions.

Why now: Growing enterprise pipeline and security questionnaire asks are introducing bespoke contract terms that require faster turnaround. Current ad-hoc approvals are creating risk (undocumented concessions), inconsistent economics, and long sales cycles.

Core components proposed:
- Delegation matrix: discount bands by customer segment (startup, mid-market, enterprise) and product bundle, with explicit authority levels (AE, AM, Sales Manager, RevOps, VP Sales). Include monetary thresholds and margin/contribution constraints.
- Auto-approval rules: low-risk standard bundles below 10% discount can auto-approve if contract template and SSO terms unchanged.
- Exception workflow: for larger discounts or custom legal/security asks, create a short review packet template that includes pricing rationale, metric impact, security questionnaire risk summary, and required signoffs.
- Audit trail: persist every approval/exception in a single source of truth (Salesforce Opportunity record + linked Confluence packet) with immutable timestamp and approver identity.
- Pricing catalog maintenance: schedule quarterly canonical catalog refreshes; changes require Product + Finance signoff and release notes to Sales.
- Integration points: RevOps to configure Salesforce flows, Finance to expose margin guardrails, Legal to own contract templates, Security to pre-clear questionnaire non-standard answers.
- Reporting and SLOs: weekly dashboard for approvals by bucket, mean time to decision, percentage of exceptions that waive standard security questionnaire answers, and regression alerts when avg discount exceeds thresholds.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Safety vs speed: tighter guardrails reduce risk but increase cycle time — proposal biases towards small auto-approvals to unblock deals and stricter review for material concessions.
- Human overhead: Delegation increases review surface area; mitigate with clear templates and RevOps automation.
- Tooling complexity: Implementing full audit immutability requires Salesforce customization and a small Confluence template micro-service — initial MVP focuses on structured fields in Opportunity and a Confluence stub.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Delegation matrix documented and approved by Sales Leadership and Finance.
- Salesforce automated approval flags for low-risk bundles (<=10% discount) implemented and tested in sandbox.
- Exception packet template available and used in three pilot deals.
- Weekly approval dashboard live and accessible to GTM leadership.

Longer-term ideas (post-MVP): dynamic price recommendations based on historical win rates, RBAC integration with Redwood Console for enterprise self-serve portals, and cryptographically signed approval artifacts for audit-heavy customers.
